answer.rationale: The line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and the contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, so a full primary switch to the low-cost vendor would meet the 18% mandate on price but introduces migration/qualification risk exactly when there is no slack to absorb a stumble; that violates the 'without increasing delivery risk' constraint and could dwarf the savings in TCO if the line stalls. Deferring is not viable because the contract does not auto-renew. The robust single move is to negotiate at renewal using the low-cost quote as benchmark leverage (memory_c4) and pursue term/volume pricing (memory_c6) while keeping the incumbent's stable integration and uninterrupted deliveries (memory_c1). This captures a meaningful portion of the mandate now, preserves the low-cost vendor as a live option and future second source (memory_c3) for the next review, and avoids committing the whole spend under pressure. I am verifying the two memories that decide the fork: whether the low-cost vendor is genuinely switch-ready (memory_c2) and whether incumbent renegotiation truly moved price and terms (memory_c4).
